Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Inspect two Replay Scrapyard saves

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

From the repository root:

Shell
nix develop --command odin build examples/replay_scrapyard/tools/inspect_run \
  -collection:godot=. -out:/tmp/replay-inspect-run
/tmp/replay-inspect-run first.replay second.replay --limit 32

The tool reads current-compatible checkpoints or complete save bundles, validates their contracts/container metadata and required image references, then compares canonical simulation fields. It accepts archives requiring a coordinator permit for read-only inspection; it cannot grant a lease or resume a session. Old content must first use the explicit save-conversion path.

Default comparison requires equal frame ticks and tick rates. Different epochs are reported in metadata and do not prevent comparing a preserved checkpoint across migration. --allow-different-ticks explicitly permits a before/after save comparison; it is not a determinism test. Tick-rate mismatch always fails.

--limit N accepts 1–256 displayed differences (default 32). The report always counts all differences and marks truncation. --public uses the public schema projection, excluding authority-only fields from the output. The default authority projection is for trusted local debugging.

The JSON report contains source paths, epoch/tick/content metadata, schema and projection, equality/truncation flags and changed field paths with values and canonical bits. Large integers remain strings so browser/JSON tools retain every bit. A pool generation, ability timer or inventory count can therefore be identified without comparing opaque whole-world hashes.

Exit codes: 0 for equal worlds, 1 for differences, 2 for invalid/incompatible input or command-line arguments. Errors go to stderr; failed validation emits no partial JSON report. Both input files remain unchanged. Reads are bounded to 16 MiB before allocation. The tool compares the simulation world, not every transport/roster or checkpoint-policy field; metadata and scope stay explicit in its output.

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_diagnostics/run.sh

The gate starts with a genuine current save, creates a separately validated checkpoint changing health, scrap, an ability timer and an unused projectile-slot generation, and checks the exact reported paths/values. It also tests equal input, truncation, explicit cross-tick comparison, corruption, obsolete content and bad limits. Hashes prove the inspection does not modify its sources.
